 Pelican Rapids Man Pleaded Guilty to Defrauding the IRS
 By Derek Sidian 
 Nov 16, 2026 | 9:39 AM 
 alexskopje / Depositphotos.com
 Pelican Rapids, MN – A Pelican Rapids man has pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud the Internal Revenue Service (IRS).
 The U.S. Department of Justice says Abdulkadir Koosaar conspired with others to defraud the IRS for the years 2020 and 2021 by aiding the preparation of more than 150 false and fraudulent income tax returns for clients.
 The conspirators, including Koosaar, included COVID-19 related sick and family leave tax credits on the returns that they knew the clients were not entitled to claim and that resulted in the returns reporting falsely inflated tax refunds. The false and fraudulent income tax returns prepared and filed by the conspirators caused a tax loss of more than $750,000.
 On Thursday, Koosaar pleaded guilty to one count of conspiring to defraud the IRS. He faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison. He also faces a period of supervised release, restitution and monetary penalties.
